verdict.rationale: Greptile documents a first-party learning system: developers can push back with 👎 reactions and explanatory reply comments, and over time it stops commenting on things the team doesn't care about. The learning is documented as gradual (2-3 weeks), with no evidence that a specific rejected comment stops recurring right away, and no independent or hands-on confirmation. Missing for 10: evidence of immediate or per-comment suppression of rejected feedback (e.g., within the same PR or the next review), detail on how replies are applied or scoped, and independent or hands-on corroboration that repeated feedback actually stops.

support.subject: As a developer, I can push back on a bad review comment and the reviewer learns — it stops repeating the same rejected feedback

citations.quote: Your 👍/👎 reactions and replies teach Greptile what matters. After 2-3 weeks, it stops commenting on things you don't care about.
Greptile learns from your team's feedback to provide increasingly relevant suggestions. The primary training methods are emoji reactions and explanatory comments.
Train Greptile with emoji reactions and feedback to improve code review relevance.
